summary: Deployed a persistent host firewall on node1 via Ansible (run from control node node4), enforcing: SSH from anywhere, TCP/9000 accepted only from node2, and TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else. Implemented with firewalld direct rules (INPUT_direct chain, ordered by priority) because node1's firewalld 0.6.3 doesn't support rich-rule priority attributes, and firewalld zone rich-rule deny/allow chains otherwise evaluate reject before accept regardless of specificity. Verified persistence across a firewalld reload and across a full node1 reboot. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all four nodes, one at a time, with boot-id proof and post-restart functional verification.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1-3 are RHEL 7.9, node4 (control_node) is Ubuntu 24.04 with ansible-core 2.20 preinstalled
Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1/2/3 using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY for the antrieb user (which has passwordless sudo)
Discovered ansible-core 2.20 requires Python >=3.9 on managed nodes; node1 only had Python 2.7 and, after install, Python 3.6 (base RHEL7 repos) then 3.8 (via RHSCL rh-python38) -- still insufficient
Created a Python venv on node4 and installed ansible-core 2.16 (supports Python 3.6+ managed nodes) to drive the playbook against node1's Python 3.6
Wrote /root/firewall-ansible/{inventory.ini,firewall.yml} on node4: installs/enables firewalld, allows the ssh service in the public zone (any source), and manages port-9000 access

Found that firewalld rich rules on this old firewalld version evaluate a zone's deny chain before its allow chain regardless of rule specificity, so a generic 'reject 9000 from anywhere' rich rule silently blocked node2 too; the 'priority' rich-rule attribute needed to fix this is unsupported on firewalld 0.6.3

Redesigned the port-9000 policy using firewalld direct rules in the INPUT_direct chain (invoked before zone processing) with explicit priorities: 0=accept from node2, 1=reject from node3, 2=reject from everyone else -- applied permanently and immediately via firewall-cmd through the command module
Verified live behavior with a test listener on node1:9000: node2 gets 200 OK, node3 and node4 get connection refused, SSH from node4 still succeeds

Ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially (node1, node2, node3, node4): captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id baseline and health, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified required state (firewalld direct rules and enforcement behavior on node1; sshd on node2/node3; ansible tooling plus a live idempotent playbook re-run confirming node1's rules survived, on node4)

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: firewall-cmd --list-all shows ssh service enabled in public zone with no source restriction (pre-existing/confirmed unchanged); SSH from node4 to node1 succeeds both before and after node1's restart
curl from node2 to node1:9000 returns HTTP 200 across three separate test runs, including after both node1's and node2's restarts
curl from node3 to node1:9000 returns connection refused across three runs, including after node1's and node3's restarts

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 rejected from everywhere else (represented by node4)
evidence.summary: curl from node4 (not node2/node3) to node1:9000 is refused both before and after node1's restart
ansible-playbook runs from control node node4 against node1 apply and then idempotently confirm the firewalld service/ssh config and INPUT_direct rules

evidence.requirement: Firewall rule persistence (survives reload and reboot)
evidence.summary: iptables -S INPUT_direct and firewall-cmd --list-all show identical rule set after `firewall-cmd --reload` and after a full node1 reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence (baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery)
evidence.summary: boot_id baseline 3dba43a5...; reboot issued and acknowledged; connection timeout confirms disruption; post-reboot boot_id db27a9e8... (changed); firewalld active with all 3 INPUT_direct rules intact; live re-test confirms node2 accept / node3 reject / SSH ok

boot_id baseline b35fad86... and sshd active; reboot issued; timeout confirms disruption; post-reboot boot_id 84aa2328... (changed), sshd active again; node2 successfully reaches node1:9000 post-restart confirming its network/service role recovered

boot_id baseline 2fc81aed... and sshd active; reboot issued; timeouts confirm disruption; post-reboot boot_id 6019753d... (changed), sshd active again; node3 still correctly rejected from node1:9000 post-restart

boot_id baseline 416c5cf5... and functional ansible-core confirmed; reboot issued; connection timeout confirms disruption; post-reboot boot_id d3668c29... (changed); ansible and the SSH keypair/playbook files survived, and a live playbook re-run against node1 confirms end-to-end orchestration and target state are both intact
